title: Infra: GPU Fleet & Capacity — Cloud Accounts, IaC Modules, CI/CD, Runbooks (Playbook Appendix)
author: Marcus Nguyen
body:
Summary
This playbook appendix consolidates operational standards and concrete runbook steps for the GPU fleet, capacity planning, cloud accounts & networking, Terraform/IaC modules, and CI/CD pipelines used by the Infra team. Use this as the canonical reference when onboarding new infra engineers, responding to capacity incidents, or proposing IaC changes that affect the GPU fleet.

Scope and audience
- Scope: all components that touch GPU provisioning and allocation (AWS/GCP accounts, networking, IaC modules, CI/CD pipelines, capacity runbooks).
- Audience: Infra engineers, SREs, platform product engineers, and on-call responders.

Ownership and escalation
- Primary owner_team: engineering (Infra).
- Service owners: gpu-provisioning (team: infra-fleet), iac-modules (team: infra-iac), infra-ci (team: infra-ci).
- On-call escalation: follow the oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process page; primary infra oncall -> infra tech lead -> Director of Infrastructure.

Key principles
1) Predictable capacity: maintain headroom for 48-hour sustained burst + 20% buffer for system churn.
2) Single source of truth: Terraform modules and remote state are the canonical configs for account/network/provisioning.
3) Safe change: every change to IaC touching GPU instance configs or autoscaling requires CI pipeline, automated tests, and a canary rollout.
4) Observable decisions: every capacity change must include cost delta, expected latency impact, and rollback plan.

GPU fleet & capacity planning
- Utilization targets and SLOs:
  - Target cluster GPU utilization (moving average 6h): 60-75% for dedicated pools, 45-60% for burst pools.
  - Hard spike SLO: 90th percentile request scheduling latency <= 250ms for < 512-token requests.
  - Cost SLOs are tracked in the Redwood Console.

- Forecasting cadence and inputs:
  1) Weekly automated forecast job (infra-forecast) pulls 30/90/365-day usage trends (embedding vs. generation load).
  2) Quarterly capacity planning meeting: product signals + sales pipeline + reserve for major rollouts.
  3) Temporary capacity: use pre-approved burst accounts and spot pools with fallback to on-demand reserved pools.

- Scaling policies and knobs:
  - Autoscaler config (defaults): min_replicas: 4, target_gpu_util_pct: 65, scale_up_step: +25% nodes, cool_down_up: 5m, cool_down_down: 10m.
  - Use predictive scaling when 6h trend exceeds 70% for two consecutive windows.

Cloud accounts & networking (account hygiene)
- Account structure:
  - Prod accounts: prod-global (primary), prod-eu, prod-apac.
  - Non-prod: staging, dev, qa, perf.
  - Shared infra accounts: security, logging, billing.

- Networking baseline:
  - VPC per-account with standardized subnet layout: public / private / data-plane.
  - GPU subnet (private) must have dedicated NAT gateway pair per-AZ and flow logs enabled.
  - Peering / Transit: production regions use Transit Gateway (AWS) or HIP (GCP) with strict route tables.

- Security & connectivity:
  - All inter-account access must go through approved peering or Transit Gateway paths.
  - Allowed egress destinations from GPU subnets: S3 endpoints, package registries, metrics/obs endpoints, and KMS endpoints only.
  - KMS keys: customer-managed keys for Private deployments; infra-managed keys for hosted.

Terraform / IaC modules and patterns
- Module catalog (high level):
  - module/gpu-cluster: GPU instance profiles, bootstrapping, node labeling, taints for workload isolation.
  - module/network-vpc: VPC / subnets / route tables / flow logs / nat gateways.
  - module/iam-roles: least-privilege IAM roles for provisioning, autoscaler, monitoring.
  - module/remote-state: remote backend config with locking (DynamoDB for AWS).

- Best practices and patterns:
  - Keep modules small and composable; each module owns a single responsibility.
  - Inputs should be primitive types or flat maps (avoid nested complex objects).
  - Outputs must include IDs and ARNs for dependent resources.
  - Module versioning: Semantic versioning; breaking changes must bump major and be documented in CHANGELOG.md.

- State & workspace strategy:
  - Remote state backends are mandatory. Prod uses S3+DynamoDB locking (AWS) or GCS+CloudSQL (GCP) equivalents.
  - Per-environment workspaces: prod, staging, dev — no ad-hoc state branches.
  - State access is restricted via IAM; human access through approved ephemeral sessions.

- Secrets and sensitive data:
  - Do NOT store secrets in TF state in plaintext. Use KMS-encrypted secret backends or external secret manager references.

CI/CD and build pipelines
- Pipeline roles/flows:
  1) Pull Request -> Terraform fmt & validate -> Unit tests for modules (terratest) -> Cost estimate job -> Plan.
  2) Plan review: Terraform plan artifacts are posted to the PR with a human-approver required for plans that touch prod GPU pools or change autoscaler thresholds.
  3) Apply: Merged changes trigger apply via an automated, environment-scoped runner with short-lived credentials.

- Pipeline configuration examples (high-level):
  - Branch protection: require PR reviews from an owning team and green pipeline.
  - Apply guardrails: requires at least two approvers for changes to prod account or GPU module.
  - Canary flow: when changing autoscaler or instance_type, create a canary cluster in staging and run smoke tests for 1 hour before promoting.

- Testing and validation:
  - Unit test modules with terratest; integration smoke tests run in staging within CI.
  - Performance regression tests: run the perf harness against a staging GPU cluster for PRs that modify runtime configuration.

Runbooks and operational playbooks
- Common incident types: capacity exhaustion, failed autoscaling, network partition to S3/registry, Terraform drift detected.

- Runbook: Capacity exhaustion (short checklist)
  1) Verify alerts: check dashboards (per-route/model latency, cluster scheduling queue length).
  2) Identify scope: which account/region/pool is affected.
  3) Short-term remediation: trigger emergency-scaling job (infra-ops/scale-up) to add N+30% nodes in the affected AZs.
  4) Medium-term: shift non-critical workloads to burst or lower-priority queues; enable additional spot pools.
  5) Post-incident: run root-cause analysis and update capacity forecasts and autoscaler knobs.

- Runbook: Failed Terraform apply (production)
  1) Halt further applies: set repo flag infra/ci/pauses/apply = true.
  2) Assess plan and error: capture plan output, identify resource conflict or API quota error.
  3) If state is inconsistent, follow state-recovery checklist: take state snapshot, create restore branch, use terraform state rm/import as needed under supervision.
  4) Only the infra-iac lead may perform state surgery; document every step in the incident ticket.

Observability and dashboards
- Required dashboards:
  - GPU Fleet Overview: capacity, utilization per-pool, queue length, preemptible/spot eviction rates.
  - Cluster Health: node ready status, pod eviction, kernel OOM kill rates, NVidia driver errors.
  - Autoscaler: scale events timeline, decision logs, duration to scale.

- Alerts (examples):
  - Scheduling queue length > 50 for > 5m -> P1 capacity.
  - Node GPU driver errors > 5% of nodes in 10m -> P1.
  - Terraform plan drift detected (checksum mismatch) -> P2.

Maintenance windows and change windows
- Scheduled maintenance: weekly 02:00-04:00 UTC Thursday for non-disruptive infra updates; major kernel/driver rollouts require a 72h announcement and canary across a single AZ first.

Team wiki and documentation hygiene
- Templates: put a runbook template and terraform-module checklist in the team-wiki root. Every new module must be accompanied by: README, inputs/outputs table, usage example, unit tests, cost estimates, and upgrade notes.
- Ownership: each module and runbook must list an owner and at least one reviewer; add those as labels on the page for easy filtering.
- Review cadence: README and runbook pages must be reviewed at least every 6 months; create a Confluence review task assigned to the owner.

Appendices
- Quick CLI snippets (examples)
  - Terraform plan for prod (example):
    export TF_VAR_env=prod && terraform init -backend-config="bucket=redwood-tfstate-prod" && terraform plan -var-file=env/prod.tfvars
  - Emergency scale-up: infra-ops scale-up --region us-west-2 --pool gpu-dedicated --add-nodes 8 --reason "oncall emergency"

- Change checklist (pull-request)
  1) Validate terratest unit results.
  2) Attach cost estimate and risk assessment.
  3) Add rollout/canary plan and rollback steps in the PR description.
  4) Assign approvers: module owner + infra lead.
